title: Add initial workload suite schema + runner CLI (v0)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Motivation: Q1’26 baseline work needs a locked, reproducible workload definition and a standard runner entrypoint. This PR introduces the initial (v0) workload suite schema + validation, and a minimal runner CLI that can execute workloads locally and emit a stable output JSON artifact for downstream ingestion (perf-canary + dashboards). Scope in this PR: (1) WorkloadSpec schema (YAML/JSON) for defining traffic shape and execution phases, (2) config validation (schema + semantic checks), (3) runner CLI (benchlab) with a local executor, (4) output artifact JSON schema + writer, (5) example workloads to unblock early variance studies. Non-goals: multi-region orchestration, fleet env pinning, and perf-canary integration (follow-ups tracked in ENG-4827 / ENG-4830).

WorkloadSpec v0: Workloads are defined as a sequence of phases (warmup, measure, cooldown) with explicit request distributions and concurrency controls. Key fields include: model (catalog name + optional revision), mode (streaming|non_streaming), prompt_tokens distribution (fixed|lognormal|explicit_bucketed), max_output_tokens distribution, concurrency (fixed|ramp), duration_s, request_rate (optional), cache_policy (cold|warm_prefix|mixed), and seeds (required for all stochastic generators). The schema is JSON Schema draft-07 stored in-repo and used for validation.

Runner CLI: New `benchlab run --workload <path> --out <dir> --runtime-endpoint <url>` command. Supports local process mode (talks to a runtime endpoint over HTTP) and a dry-run mode for validating/previewing the generated traffic plan. Emits a single `run.json` artifact per workload invocation.

Validation: Two layers: (a) JSON Schema validation for shape, required fields, enums, etc.; (b) semantic validation for guardrails (e.g., duration_s > 0, ramp endpoints sane, bucket weights sum to 1, streaming requires chunk_size_tokens, seeds present, max_output_tokens bounded). Validation errors are designed to be copy/pasteable into Linear/Slack and include JSON pointer paths.

Output artifact: Adds a stable `benchmark-lab run artifact` JSON format (versioned with `artifact_version: "0.1"`). Includes: workload metadata (name, hash, schema version), runner metadata (git_sha, build timestamp), environment metadata (host, region if provided, GPU name if detectable, driver/CUDA strings if provided), request plan summary, and metrics (TTFT/TPOT/latency/throughput) aggregated at p50/p95/p99 plus error counters. Raw per-request samples are optional and off by default (to avoid huge artifacts).

Examples: Adds example workloads under `examples/workloads/` to anchor the taxonomy work: `chat_streaming_short.yaml`, `chat_nonstreaming_medium.yaml`, `long_context_streaming.yaml`, and `bursty_concurrency_mixed_prompts.yaml`. Prompts are synthetic placeholders; no customer text.

Illustrative config snippet (examples/workloads/chat_streaming_short.yaml): name: chat_streaming_short; mode: streaming; phases: [warmup 30s @ concurrency 16, measure 180s @ concurrency 32]; prompt_tokens: lognormal(mean=220, sigma=0.55, min=16, max=768); max_output_tokens: fixed(256); cache_policy: warm_prefix(share_prefix_ratio=0.35); seeds: {plan: 1337, prompts: 42}.

Notes for reviewers: I tried to keep schema minimal but forward-compatible. Artifact versioning is intentionally explicit so we can lock baseline runs to a known producer/consumer contract. Metrics are runner-side aggregation from client-perceived timings; server-side telemetry correlation is out of scope here (ENG-4832).

Test plan: `pytest -q` locally; added unit tests for schema validation, semantic validation, and artifact writer; ran `benchlab run` against staging runtime endpoint and confirmed artifact parses with `tools/validate_artifact.py`.
commits: spec: add WorkloadSpec JSON Schema draft-07 and loader
cli: introduce benchlab command group and `run` subcommand
runner: add traffic plan generators (fixed/lognormal/bucketed) + concurrency ramp
validation: semantic checks with JSON pointer error messages
artifact: define run output schema v0.1 + writer + validator tool
examples: add initial workload suite examples (synthetic prompts)
conversation:
Marcus Reed (review): Can we make seeds mandatory? Otherwise we’ll never get repeatable variance measurements. Also please ensure we hash the resolved workload (after defaults) not the raw file.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Agree. Updated schema + semantic validation to require `seeds.plan` and `seeds.prompts`. Also changed workload hash to be computed from the normalized/fully-resolved spec (post-defaults) and included `workload_hash` in the artifact.

Sana Farid (review): For variance studies, we need the artifact to include trial count and whether this run is warm/cold cache. Right now cache_policy is in the input but not surfaced clearly in the output summary.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `plan_summary.cache_policy` and `plan_summary.trials` to artifact. The runner currently runs a single trial per invocation; keeping the field so we can expand to multiple trials without breaking consumers.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please add a place for environment pinning data (driver/CUDA/runtime build). Even if the runner can’t enforce it yet, we need it stamped so we can debug fleet drift.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `env.cuda_version`, `env.driver_version`, and `runner.git_sha` fields. The CLI supports overriding these via flags for now; auto-detection is best-effort. Follow-up for hard enforcement will live in ENG-4834.

Connor O'Brien (review): Output JSON needs to be stable/contracted; can we version it and add a validator in-tree? Also recommend avoiding per-request samples by default.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Done: `artifact_version: 0.1` and `tools/validate_artifact.py`. Per-request samples are gated behind `--include-samples` and default off.

Claire Dubois (review): Examples look good, but please ensure none of the prompts resemble customer text. Maybe add an explicit README note.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added note in README + comments in examples that prompts must be synthetic/sanitized.

CI note: Initial run failed pyright due to missing exports in `artifact/__init__.py`; fixed in follow-up commit. Final checks green.

Approved-by: Marcus Reed, Sana Farid, Sean Gallagher. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: introduces v0 workload spec + runner CLI for perf baseline suite; produces versioned run artifacts for perf-canary ingestion (not yet wired).
